score.note: Assigned to the shop/select_party_member.c family by clustering, but this owner is an inventory-menu equip/transfer confirmation dialog operating on Data_03001f2c (it sits between the already-named inventory_menu owners 080a51d0 and 080a5534 in source-paths.json), not a party-member picker. It shares the template's for(;;)/redraw/Modulo-wraparound Yes-No idiom with sibling 080a524c but adds an owner-state snapshot/restore around the confirmation: Runtime_GetObject(menu->target_owner) fetches the acting owner's inventory record, Mem_Copy (Func_080072f0, 4-arg form: dst,src,size,desc) backs it up into a Runtime_BumpAllocate'd 0x14C-byte scratch block before the dialog runs, Func_08077050 tests item/owner compatibility to decide whether to even show the dialog (skipping straight to a rejection sound 175 and forced selection=1 when incompatible), and on a 'No' outcome the snapshot is copied back over the live owner record before the scratch block is freed and BattleUnit_Recalculate/Func_080772c0 refresh derived stats. The candidate reproduces this whole shape and call sequence but is 40 bytes shorter than the reference (388 vs 428): the reference's prologue saves four high registers (fp, sl, r9, r8 -- i.e. it keeps 7 registers, r5..r9/sl/fp, simultaneously live across calls), while the candidate's register allocation only needed 3 (sl, r9, r8), meaning at least one more value in the real source stays live across a call boundary than in this draft -- most likely the target_owner byte or the message id used for the second UiText_DrawAt draw is re-read from a live register in the reference rather than re-loaded from the struct byte each time as this draft does. This is a source-shape gap (an under-modeled live variable), not something I chased down to an exact fix given the time remaining.

rejected_experiments.reason: Initially read the ROM's `bl Func_080072f0` call with only 3 visible register-setup instructions (r0=K,r1=ownerState,r2=332) and assumed a 3-arg memcpy-like signature with the fixed global 0x03001388 as the destination. games/gs1/include/runtime_mem.h already declares `void Func_080072f0(void *dst, void *src, s32 size, void *desc)` (Mem_Copy) as 4-arg; re-reading the raw asm showed r0 was never reloaded before the call (it still held Runtime_BumpAllocate's return value from two instructions earlier), so the real args are (dst=bump-allocated buffer, src=ownerState, size=332, desc=0x03001388) -- the bump-allocated buffer is the snapshot destination, not an unused scratch. Fixed by switching to the 4-arg Mem_Copy from the header; this changed the function's behavior (the snapshot is now actually populated) but the resulting candidate is still not byte-exact.

Declared a local `Func_08004938` prototype returning `void *`; games/gs1/include/runtime_mem.h already declares `u32 Runtime_BumpAllocate(s32 size)` (u32 return, not pointer) and is used everywhere else in the codebase that way. Switched to the header's declaration and cast at each use site to match.
